title: How dams make electricity
examples: How does the water actually turn the machine?
What part of the dam makes the electricity?
Is the water used for anything else besides power?

explain.say: First we look at stored water behind the dam.
The stored water has energy because it is held high up.
Next the water rushes through tunnels to the turbines.
The fast moving water spins the large blades called turbines.

draw.text: Turbines: Water's force spins the blades

explain.say: The spinning turbine is connected to a generator to make power.
In real life, this process powers our homes and schools.

faq.q: Does the water have to fall a very long way?
faq.a: Yes, the greater the drop, the more energy the water has. This helps spin the turbine more strongly.
asks: Does the drop affect the power?

faq.q: What is the generator actually doing?
faq.a: The generator uses the spinning motion to create an electrical current. It works by moving magnets near wires.
No, dams often create reservoirs that can also be used for drinking water or controlling floods.
asks: Are there other uses for dams?

faq.q: Does the water need to be clean to work well?
faq.a: Yes, while the process works with moving water, the overall health of the river is important for the ecosystem.

faq.q: What happens to the water after it passes the turbine?
faq.a: The water usually flows out downstream, often returning to the river's natural path. It has lost most of its energy.
asks: Is the river normal after the dam?

facts: Potential energy is stored energy due to height.
Turbines are machines that spin when hit by moving fluid.
Generators convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.
The force of falling water turns the turbine blades.

quiz.say: What type of energy is stored in the water behind the dam?
quiz.why: The water is held high up, giving it stored energy due to its height.

wrong.0: Chemical energy is stored in bonds, like in batteries, not in height.
wrong.1: Electrical energy is what is made at the end, not what is stored at the start.
wrong.3: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, which the water has after it falls.

quiz.say: What connects the spinning turbine to the electricity making part?
quiz.why: The shaft acts like a rod, transferring the spinning force from the turbine to the generator.

wrong.1: The pipe guides the water, but the shaft transfers the rotation.
wrong.2: Wires carry electricity, but the shaft carries the physical spin.
wrong.3: Gears change the speed, but the shaft is the main connecting rod.

quiz.say: If the water level drops, what happens to the electricity made?
quiz.why: Less falling water means less force on the turbine, making less electricity.

wrong.0: A drop in water level means less force, so power decreases.
wrong.1: The power output depends directly on the force of the falling water.
wrong.3: Even a small flow can still generate some electricity.
